To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CBL is inhibited by AVG in a slow, time-dependent, irreversible manner, and that the structure of the C-terminal domain of the enzyme, which is not involved in catalysis, is important for binding of the inhibitor.
the natural toxin rhizobitoin and its structural analogue l-aminoethoxynylglycine are potent, slowly binding inhibitors of CBL.

the PLP-dependent enzyme CBL is inhibited by AVG in a slow-binding manner, and that the X-ray crystal structure of the CblAVG complex reveals the binding of AVG to CBL in a way similar to that of cystathionine, but after abstraction of the alpha-proton, the reaction proceeds to a CBL nongeneric dead-end product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhibition of CBL by AVG and MVG.
the elucidation of the reaction mechanism of PLP-dependent enzymes and with the development of novel, specific, and irreversible inhibitors of these enzymes.
the elucidation of the mechanism of the slow-binding inhibition of E. coli CBL by AVG and the structural characterization of the resulting enzyme-inhibitor adduct by X-ray crystallographic analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition mechanism of AVG is similar to that of the substrate cysteine.
CBL is inhibited by AVG and rhizobitoin through a slow binding mechanism, in which the inhibitor binds in the active site and is transformed into a dead-end product.
the inhibition by rhizobitoxic compounds is a result of the reaction of these compounds with CBL in the presence of PLP, which is followed by slow protonation of the C4' atom of PLP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rhizobitoxicin and AVG are slow-binding inhibitors of CBL, and the inhibition mechanism is the same for both inhibitors.
the inhibition of CBL by the vinylglycines AVG and rhizobitotoxine is caused by an irreversible reaction of the inhibitor with the active site of the enzyme.

CBLAVG is a "slow-binding" inhibitor that binds in a similar manner to CBL as cysteine but in a different reaction step, i.e. after abstraction of alpha-proton, resulting in the formation of a ketimine PLPC4' adduct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CBL can be inhibited by a slow-binding mechanism.
the CBL inhibitor AVG is an example of a slow-binding inhibitor that binds in a similar fashion to the substrate.
the inhibition of CBL by AVG and rhizobitoin can be rationalized in the same manner as the inhibition of serine racemase by AVG.
